title: How were films such as "Maladolescenza" (1977) & "Piccole labbra" (1978) allowed to be produced?

commenti.body: I was shocked when I watched Roman Polanski's *MacBeth* and there's a scene where MacDuff's wife is bathing her son and it's literally some 10 year old kid with his penis out. I'm sure there's a joke about Polanski somewhere in there but yeah, it seemed super unnecessary to me even if it wasn't sexualized

Sounds like a case of what one might consider "incidental" child nudity, which isn't very uncommon - can still be shocking/distasteful. My concern lies more with nudity & interactions in a directly sexual context.

With the lifting of pornography bans in a number of countries everything was de facto legalized for a little while for some filmmakers. That’s really all there is to it frankly, they could so they did. It’s simply the exploitation filmmaker urge to do something more EXTREME and attention grabbing at the end of the day.

OP, are you trying to write a piece based on the responses you get? This is the second time I see this post, I saw the same post in r/AskHistorians, and I see you have made a couple more posts/enquiries on the same matter but in other subs.
I got the US perspective on r/AskHistorians, I'm looking for something more specific to European cinema. Plus, this community is specialised for film.
